title: Temporal control surfaces: anatomy, clock physics, and learned computation
summary: September 24 brings the neuron-inspired line closer to explicit neurobiological constraints without treating the toy mechanisms as cortical identity claims. KolmeOvea puts three physically distinct control surfaces into one pyramidal-cell abstraction—apical/context, basket/timing, and chandelier/AIS publication—and its trained subfolder asks which jobs gradient descent actually assigns to them. FrequencyAndNeurons follows the basket branch upstream by removing the imposed pacemaker and testing what sets an emergent PING gamma period. GATGRILS follows the learned/instrument branch: its gauge-aware probes and causal interventions ask whether task learning discovers clean operator/admission/publication roles. TATWATASW moves the weak apical-inference result into a learning-side test: a BTSP-style plateau writes an anticipatory predictive field, while rhythmic phase compression plus fast plasticity writes directional order only when dead time protects the arrow. Rytmi then closes those pieces into one measured sequence machine: plateau-shaped asymmetric fields drive emergent precession against rhythmic inhibition, STDP writes the ordered chain, and replay shows that dead time also suppresses spurious second waves under noise. TransformerToX opens a parallel engineering branch from transformers back toward resident temporal computation: Gate 0 exactly rewrites one frozen causal attention head as address and write geometry, while fixed-state temporal memories are implemented but their matched-budget Gate 1 comparison remains deliberately unfinished. The genealogy therefore records a fork, not a collapse: clock physics, circuit control surfaces, learning windows, replay dynamics, operator translation, and external computation tomography are adjacent questions that constrain one another but are not the same mechanism.

nodes.claim: Places apical/context control, basket/perisomatic timing, and chandelier/AIS publication on three distinct control surfaces of one pyramidal-cell-inspired circuit, then asks in KolmeOveav1 whether training assigns those surfaces distinct jobs.
nodes.survived: The hand-built v0 cleanly separates the three intervention locations under matched replacement controls. In the trained follow-up, the AIS/output gate specializes robustly in all reported conditions and seeds; the basket gate becomes necessary when it alone has access to phase, and top-down basket modulation matters when cue/context has no direct soma route. This supports access and physical intervention location as important determinants of learned control use.
nodes.killed: Architecture alone did not make all three doors spontaneously specialize. The apical gain remained marginal, basket specialization depended on access constraints, and the preregistered survival rule did not correctly account for downstream functions. V0 is a known-answer construction and v1 is a small trained toy; neither establishes these abstract roles as the biological functions of apical tuft, basket cells, or chandelier cells.

nodes.claim: Tests whether an emergent PING gamma rhythm is set by local E-I biophysics or by the number of phase slots a computation would like to multiplex.
nodes.survived: Across the frozen sweeps, slowing GABA_A decay slows the rhythm strongly, stronger excitatory drive speeds it, and splitting fixed total drive across 1 to 16 input streams leaves frequency essentially flat. The firing window stays only about 1.9-3.4 ms while the period expands about 3.6-fold, so slower inhibition mainly buys silent recovery time rather than proportionally wider admission slots.
nodes.killed: The tested local PING loop does not sense slot demand and does not retune its gamma frequency to accommodate more streams. The result is limited to the mean-field PING model used here: it does not establish a universal cortical gamma law and does not address ING, mixed regimes, theta generation, spatial circuitry, or load-sensing mechanisms outside the loop.

nodes.claim: Uses gauge-aware local response descriptors, temporal grammar, neutral pings, and causal transplants to ask what computation a learned recurrent system carries through time and whether operator, admission, and publication become distinct learned jobs.
nodes.survived: V0 preserves exact behavior and temporal grammar under invertible hidden-state basis changes, establishing a usable gauge-control harness even though its stronger forecasting claim failed. In corrected v1, cycle-mean replacement damages the learned rhythmic admission profile just beyond the frozen threshold (median 0.151), and the strongest secondary result is a silent-ping assay: resident operator, phase, and route factors decode at 1.0/1.0/1.0 from the neutral-ping response and fall to 0.5/0.5/0.5 after resident-state reset.
nodes.killed: V0 did not meet its preregistered predictive superiority gate. V1 did not demonstrate the proposed three-way operator/admission/publication specialization: only 4/12 canonical seeds were task-valid, transplant specificity was weak, publication was not a clean independent route controller, and the overall frozen verdict remained FAIL. This is evidence about the tested learned system, not a negative claim about biological cortex.

nodes.claim: Separates two candidate learning roles for temporal cortical machinery: a BTSP-style plateau writes a predictive field around an instructive event, while phase-compressed rhythmic windows plus fast plasticity write directional order.
nodes.survived: E1 gives the imposed asymmetric plateau rule a predictive field shifted before the plateau, while symmetric-window and plain-Hebbian controls stay centered. E3 then shows that imposed theta phase precession can compress a slow series into an STDP-writable order, with much stronger forward drive and predominantly forward replay across the frozen gain/threshold grid. FrequencyAndNeurons' dead time becomes load-bearing here: reserving a silent part of each cycle prevents cross-cycle wrap-around pairs from cancelling the learned arrow.
nodes.killed: A single plateau per cell does not, on its own, write a robust directional sequence: in E2 recurrent replay is overwhelmingly bidirectional and forward-only replay is rare. Slower theta also does not increase the tested sequence reach, and the fields, plateau times, phase precession and theta rhythm are imposed rather than emergent. The repo therefore does not establish a cortical sequence-writing mechanism or that apical tuft alone carries order.

nodes.claim: Combines plateau-written asymmetric fields, rhythmic inhibition, emergent phase precession, local STDP, and forward replay into one brain-inspired sequence machine, then tests how long chains survive and what rhythmic dead time contributes during recall.
nodes.survived: R1 makes phase precession emerge from plateau-written drive against rhythmic inhibition rather than imposing a phase variable; plain STDP then reaches 0.95 forward-only in-order replay in the main condition, while phase shuffling collapses ordered replay. G0 shows that one cue can carry an 80-item lap with median in-order reach 79 in the noiseless grid. Under stronger replay noise, rhythmic dead time plus re-cueing suppresses spurious second waves and improves long-chain order, giving dead time a second measured job in addition to protecting the learning arrow.
nodes.killed: One-shot capacity has not been shown: R1 learns over 20 laps, and G1 remains future work. Plateau locations, upstream place inputs, and the shared theta rhythm are still imposed, so self-chosen surprise-triggered plateaus are also not demonstrated. Precession is partial at about 0.2 cycle, and re-cueing is not a free improvement: on noiseless 80-item replay it performs worse than one cue. The repo therefore does not yet establish a general sequence learner or an AI replacement for attention/SSMs.

nodes.claim: Compiles one frozen causal transformer head into explicit address geometry M=W_Q W_K^T and write geometry N=W_V W_O, then prepares matched-budget fixed-state memories for asking whether token history can become resident temporal state.
nodes.survived: Gate 0 is an exact zero-fit algebraic compiler on the frozen deterministic head: 32 cases use zero learned parameters, with maximum logit error 1.78e-15, maximum output error 1.33e-15, and aggregate output relative RMSE 3.43e-16. The v0 also implements bounded static, decay, and resonant memory primitives with explicit scalar-budget accounting and no raw-history cache.
nodes.killed: Gate 1 is not a result yet: the held-out matched-budget evaluator and frozen Gate 1 receipt are intentionally absent, so the repo has not shown that temporal resident memory beats the matched static attacker. Gate 0 does not compress KV history, remove softmax, establish an efficiency advantage, validate a pretrained-model adapter, or make a biological identity claim.

edges.why: KolmeOvea explicitly starts from NewMachine's result that control channels collapse in a static scalar setting, then adds compartments, time/phase, and output-route structure to make the three intervention surfaces physically non-equivalent.
OperatorTime supplied the resident-history/effective-operator language that KolmeOvea places on the apical/context side of the circuit-level three-door picture.

FrequencyAndNeurons is explicitly a closed side question raised by KolmeOvea's imposed basket rhythm: it replaces the pacemaker with an emergent E-I PING loop and asks what actually sets the period and admission window.

GATGRILS v1 carries the SilentPing question into a task-trained recurrent system: a fixed neutral ping reads resident information that disappears to chance after state reset, without making the ping itself item-specific.

GATGRILS operationalizes the gauge-aware computation-coordinate problem in a learned recurrent system, retaining explicit invertible hidden-state basis attacks and local response grammar rather than treating raw hidden coordinates as the computation.

The two repositories independently test the same operator/admission/publication decomposition from opposite directions: KolmeOvea begins with physically separated control surfaces and then trains them, while GATGRILS begins with a learned recurrent system and asks whether causal interventions recover a clean three-way organization. Both caution against assuming the decomposition emerges automatically, while timing remains the strongest shared survivor.

TATWATASW explicitly reuses FrequencyAndNeurons' dead-time result as a learning constraint: when phase-compressed spikes fill the whole theta cycle, cross-cycle wrap-around pairs write backward links and erase the directional bias; reserving an inhibitory silent interval protects directional STDP.

KolmeOvea's trained follow-up found the apical door weak when tested as an inference-time gain. TATWATASW moves that control surface to learning, using a plateau-gated BTSP-style window to write predictive fields; its failure to write a directional chain by itself keeps the correction bounded rather than declaring apical control unimportant.

GATGRILS found silent resident state readable by ping but no clean three-way inference specialization. TATWATASW attacks the complementary learning-side question: plateau plasticity writes anticipatory field structure while temporal order comes from rhythmic compression plus dead time, separating what a resident state can reveal from what the learning rule writes.

Rytmi explicitly continues TATWATASW's E1-E4 chain: its R1 makes phase precession emerge from plateau-written drive against rhythmic inhibition, then reuses the same STDP/replay machinery; G0 extends the line into long-chain and noisy recall.

Rytmi's own lineage keeps AnotherOddThing v5's fast-minus-slow temporal-direction result as the local-phase precursor: two local leaky traces can distinguish temporal direction without being handed a symbolic phase coordinate, even though R1 ultimately finds that rhythmic inhibition itself can provide the needed dead interval in its working regime.

The repositories attack the same broader translation from explicit event history toward local temporal machinery from opposite sides. TATWATASW asks how windows, phase and local plasticity turn event timing into resident sequence structure; TransformerToX starts from an exact attention-head compiler and asks whether explicit KV history can later be replaced by bounded resident temporal state. This records conceptual convergence, not direct implementation ancestry.

TransformerToX explicitly reserves Gate 2 for the AnotherOddThing v5 question: can two histories with matched present amplitude be separated by locally accumulated temporal direction or phase without an externally supplied symbolic position variable?
